And at first, forces small in number came into the vicinity of Aleppo,
and Malik Mu'azzam the elder, son of Saladin the Great, went out and encountered them,
and he was broken,
and he fled and entered Aleppo.
And those Tatars crossed over and went and destroyed the city of Ma'arrat [al-Nu'man],
and they went against Hama,
and they surrendered it peacefully;
and likewise to Homs.
And Malik Nasir took his wives, his sons, and his servants and departed from Damascus,
and he fled to the desert of Kerak and Shawbak.
And the Tatars went against Damascus,
and its lords surrendered it peacefully,
and nothing evil happened to them.
Against Aleppo, however, the King of Kings himself camped in person,
and he commanded, and walls were built outside the wall of Aleppo around the entire large perimeter.
And they waged fierce warfare against it,
and after not many days,
they gained mastery over the walls from the side of the Iraq Gate,
and they entered Aleppo on Sunday, the eve of the Fast of Nineveh, the 23rd
of the Latter Kanun of the said year.
And there was in Aleppo slaughter like that in Baghdad, and even more.
And because the Ba'albakkites had destroyed the roof of the walls of our church which was in it,
and I, the feeble one,
who was metropolitan in it,
from fear of these things had gone out to go to the service of the King of Kings,
and was shut up in Qal'at Najm,
our believers, the people who were in Aleppo, were left without a head,
and most of them gathered in the church of the Greeks.
And the Tatars came in upon them,
and killed them and took their families captive.
And at the end, Thoros, the Armenian priest,
the nephew of Catholicos Mar Constantine,
along with the monk Kurak entered and set free whoever they found {OCR?} alive,
and gathered them into our church.
And when they took the city, [and] the Tatars entered the city {OCR?},
they fought against the citadel,
and they took it too peacefully.
And from there the King of Kings went against Harem,
and sought of them that they surrender,
and that he would swear to them that he would not harm them.
And those foolish ones replied:
"Since you are a king whose religion is unknown,
by what shall we make you swear? Unless Fakhr al-Din, the governor of the citadel of Aleppo, swears to us
